titleText.es: Al tercer trimestre tendrás cientos de bebés dentro de ti.
titleText.en: By the third trimester, there will be hundreds of babies inside you.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive closely translates the official title text and preserves the same deliberately reckless extrapolation joke.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to extrapolate; to extend a trend beyond the known data
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Extrapolar means using an observed pattern to estimate what lies outside the observations already available.

example.es: No conviene extrapolar una tendencia a partir de dos datos.
example.en: It is unwise to extrapolate a trend from two data points.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: of the; introduces the period after a finales
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Del combines de and el. In a finales del mes, it connects a finales to the masculine period mes; natural English usually renders the complete expression as ‘late in the month’ or ‘at the end of the month.’

example.en: We will return late in the summer.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Tendrás is the future form of tener for one familiar person. Tener changes its future stem to tendr- before the ending -ás.

example.en: Tomorrow you will have more time.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; links an evaluation with the recommended action
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After es, será, or sería mejor, que introduces the action judged preferable. Spanish then uses a specially changed verb form for that recommendation.

example.en: It will be better for us to leave early.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: you try; you attempt (special form after a recommendation)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Intentes is a changed form of intentar for one familiar person. It appears here because the action is recommended after será mejor que rather than stated as a fact.

example.en: It is better for you to try to rest.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: A mayorista sells large quantities to businesses rather than individual retail customers. After de in precios de mayorista, it describes wholesale-level prices.

example.es: La tienda compra la fruta a un mayorista.
example.en: The shop buys the fruit from a wholesaler.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: for; introduces the product that a price or rate applies to
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After a word such as precio or tarifa, para can introduce the item or service whose price is being discussed.

example.es: Pedimos una tarifa para el servicio completo.
example.en: We asked for a rate for the complete service.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can you introduce a conclusion that the other person can supposedly see from the evidence?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use como puedes ver, meaning ‘as you can see.’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Como means ‘as,’ puedes means ‘you can,’ and ver stays in its unchanged dictionary form after puedes. The phrase often introduces an explanation or claimed conclusion.

example.es: Como puedes ver, la puerta está abierta.
example.en: As you can see, the door is open.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that it is or will be better for someone to do something?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the needed form of ser, then mejor que, and change the following action verb to the form used for a recommendation.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The form of ser can show the time: es mejor que, será mejor que, or sería mejor que. Because the following action is being judged preferable rather than reported as a fact, its verb takes a special subjunctive form such as llegues, salgamos, or intenten.

example.en: It is better for you to arrive early.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you refer to a wholesale price rather than a retail price?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use precio de mayorista, or precios de mayorista in the plural.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: De links precio to mayorista, the wholesale level or seller category. The first noun changes for number, while mayorista keeps the same written form here.

example.es: La empresa ofrece precios de mayorista.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: Say pastel de boda; use pasteles de boda for more than one.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: De connects pastel to the kind of event it is made for. Spanish does not turn boda into an adjective.

example.es: Encargaron un pastel de boda pequeño.
example.en: They ordered a small wedding cake.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: extrapolar · ayer · hoy · más de cincuenta maridos
cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why is the graph's prediction absurd?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: It draws a straight trend through only two observations—zero husbands yesterday and one today—and extends that line far beyond the observed time. Two points always determine a line, but they provide almost no evidence that the real situation will continue linearly.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The title text repeats the same error with pregnancy: it projects a rapidly growing count into a later trimester as though every short-term change must continue unchanged.

applications.explanationEn: Como introduces the claimed visible conclusion, puedes changes for one familiar listener, and ver stays in its unchanged dictionary form after puedes.
A finales del introduces the period's late part, and próximo mes supplies the complete period being located in time.
Próximo uses its masculine singular ending -o to match the masculine singular noun mes.
Tener uses its irregular future stem tendr- and adds -ás for one familiar listener.
Más de marks a numerical threshold being exceeded, while cincuenta maridos supplies the full quantity.
Será places the evaluation in future time, mejor states what is preferable, que introduces the recommended action, and intentes is the changed recommendation form of intentar.
Ser keeps its full dictionary form and adds -á for a future statement about one person or thing.
Intentes changes to fit the recommendation, while conseguir follows directly in its unchanged dictionary form as the action to attempt.
Precios names the rates, de links them to their commercial category, and mayorista identifies the wholesale level.
Pasteles is plural for multiple cakes, and de boda identifies the event they are made for.
